_meta.description: Edge Assessment – short work scenarios that estimate judgment (critical_thinking) and responsibility (ownership). Each option gives preset points 0-3. Results are ESTIMATES, shown to the user as such, never used to make hiring decisions.
_meta.status: DRAFT – the team should review/rewrite every scenario and add field-specific versions (Electrical / IT / Business).

questions.text: An AI tool gives you a design (code, wiring layout or report) that looks correct. The deadline is tomorrow. What do you do?

options.text: Submit it as is – the AI is usually right.
Skim it quickly and submit.
Check the parts that would cause the most damage if wrong, then submit.
Check the critical parts and tell your lead which parts were AI-generated.

questions.text: You notice a mistake in work your team already delivered to a client. Nobody else has noticed.

options.text: Stay quiet – it's already delivered.
Fix it silently in the next version.
Tell your lead and suggest a fix.
Tell your lead, estimate the impact on the client, and propose a fix.

questions.text: Two data sources give you different numbers for the same thing.

options.text: Use the one that supports your conclusion.
Average them.
Find out why they differ before using either.
Ask a colleague which one they normally use.

questions.text: Your manager asks you to take on a third project while you are already behind on two.

options.text: Say yes and work late every night.
Say no.
Explain your current workload and ask which project should be prioritised.
Accept, then quietly lower quality on all three.

questions.text: You are given a vague task: 'make our process better with AI'.

options.text: Pick the newest AI tool and start using it.
Wait until someone gives clearer instructions.
Find where the process wastes the most time, then test one small AI fix there.
Write a long report of every possible AI tool.
